filesystem.binary_and_config: root-owned and non-writable by mihver-ledger or any caller

os_identity.service_manager: Root-owned unit starts authledgerd with User=mihver-ledger, Group=mihver-ledger, NoNewPrivileges, private temporary directories, a read-only executable tree, and write access only to /var/lib/mihver/auth-ledger and /run/mihver/auth-ledger.

architecture.separation: A standalone process structurally and operationally separate from Publication Broker and all execution-tier components.

authorization_grants.consume_once_state: The ledger schema may record unused/consumed status and a unique consumption transaction for ALLOW_ONCE, but V1C has no callable production checkAndConsume endpoint and no component may use this state to trigger or authorize an effect.
authorization_grants.issuance_checks: Issuance requires already-imported valid evidence, an active matching Council epoch, current stopEpoch capture inside the same write transaction, bounded validity, uniqueness of grantId, and no wildcard subject, operation, target, evidence, or epoch fields.
authorization_grants.issuer: Only an authenticated human R3 administrator using grant-admin.sock may create or revoke a grant.
authorization_grants.validation: A grant is valid only when every requested binding matches exactly, time bounds hold, evidence and Council epoch remain acceptable, the grant is not revoked, and grant.issuanceStopEpoch equals the current global stopEpoch.

council_and_evidence_boundary.import: The evidence importer submits original supported evidence bytes plus declared media type and provenance metadata. authledgerd performs bounded parsing, schema validation, canonicalization, Council-epoch lookup, signature/quorum validation, replay checks, and digest computation itself.
council_and_evidence_boundary.registry: CouncilEpochRegistry is stored inside the ledger database and contains epoch ID, exact member/key set, signature policy, activation state, canonicalization version, and registry-record digest.
council_and_evidence_boundary.registry_authority: Only registry-admin.sock may mutate it. Grant administrators, evidence importers, clients, Publication Broker, Claude, and Codex cannot do so.
council_and_evidence_boundary.stored_result: Accepted evidence stores immutable original-byte digest, canonical-byte digest, canonicalization version, validated Council epoch, verified signer identities, validation result, and import transaction ID.
council_and_evidence_boundary.trust_rule: A caller-supplied digest, parsed object, approval flag, signer list, or hash-shaped artifact is never trusted as evidence. Unsupported, ambiguous, non-canonical, unknown-epoch, expired, or invalidly signed evidence is rejected and audited.

ipc_and_capabilities.ai_exclusion: Claude, Codex, their service accounts, and their worker processes are members only of mihver-ledger-client when read access is required. They are never members of any privileged group, receive no privileged socket file descriptor, and cannot issue grants, import trusted evidence, mutate the Council registry, or change stopEpoch.
ipc_and_capabilities.peer_authentication: Every accepted Unix-domain connection is authorized from kernel SO_PEERCRED UID/GID. Caller-supplied identity or role fields are ignored. Authorization is checked again per RPC.
ipc_and_capabilities.role_isolation: The four privileged groups have no implicit cross-membership. authledgerd maps each socket to a compile-time RPC allowlist and also validates peer credentials, so access to one administrative socket grants no other capability.

stop_epoch.corruption_or_ambiguity: On integrity failure, unreadable WAL, missing or ambiguous singleton state, unauthorized file ownership/mode, or uncertain recovery, authledgerd opens no sockets and enters global-stop failure. It never guesses, resets, or recreates the register. Recovery is an offline root-controlled incident procedure using preserved database/WAL material and audited backups; service resumes only with a demonstrably non-decreasing epoch. If the prior high-water value cannot be established, the ledger remains unavailable rather than selecting a value.
stop_epoch.increment: authledgerd executes BEGIN IMMEDIATE; reads the singleton; rejects UINT64_MAX; updates epoch to exactly old+1 using a guarded WHERE epoch=old clause; inserts the audit row; commits; then returns the committed epoch. Concurrent requests serialize on SQLite's writer lock, and a zero-row guarded update is retried or rejected without success.
stop_epoch.no_reset_path: There is no decrement, set, reset, delete, import, database-reinitialize, or epoch-override RPC. Neither ADMIN nor CLIENT protocols define such an operation. SQLite files are inaccessible to normal administrators and clients; only the daemon OS user can write them, while root is explicitly part of the machine TCB.
stop_epoch.owner: authledgerd is the sole database writer; mutation authority is exclusively the OS role mihver-stop-operator through stop-admin.sock.
stop_epoch.persistence: The committed value resides in ledger.sqlite3 and WAL under synchronous=FULL. Startup completes WAL recovery, verifies schema and singleton cardinality, runs integrity checks, and reads stopEpoch before opening any socket.
stop_epoch.representation: A singleton row keyed by the fixed name GLOBAL_STOP with an unsigned 64-bit epoch, schema version, and last mutation transaction ID. Missing rows, duplicates, invalid types, overflow, or values outside range are fatal.
stop_epoch.stale_rejection: All grant issuance records the epoch read transactionally. Every later validation rejects when issuanceStopEpoch differs from current stopEpoch, so one increment invalidates every earlier grant.

storage_and_transactions.audit: Append-only audit rows include transaction ID, authenticated peer UID, authorized role, operation, canonical request digest, prior and resulting state identifiers, timestamp, and result. UPDATE and DELETE are denied for audit rows by application invariants and startup schema verification.
storage_and_transactions.engine: SQLite with WAL, foreign_keys=ON, synchronous=FULL, trusted_schema=OFF, defensive mode enabled, and a single authledgerd writer.
storage_and_transactions.write_rule: Every state mutation and its audit event commit in the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Failed commits produce neither state nor success receipts.

zero_execution_effect_consumers.dormant_future_interface: A non-installed interface specification may reserve atomic checkAndConsume semantics, but it has no socket route, credentials, caller, deployment unit, or effect binding in V1C. Enabling any V1D consumer requires a separate ADR covering consumer identity, effect binding, crash semantics, replay behavior, and rollout.
zero_execution_effect_consumers.enforcement: checkAndConsume is absent from all installed V1C socket dispatch tables and client libraries. Build/deployment tests reject that RPC symbol or an execution dependency on authledgerd outside read-only validation and observability paths.
zero_execution_effect_consumers.v1c_invariant: At V1C exit, no production execution-tier component, Publication Broker, agent, plugin, worker, or client calls checkAndConsume or consumes ALLOW_ONCE state to perform any external or local effect.

proposalContent.summary: Adopt a dedicated, fail-closed Authorization Ledger daemon with OS-enforced role separation, transactional SQLite/WAL state, privileged canonical evidence import, exact-bound human R3 grants, and a persistent monotonic stopEpoch. V1C stores ALLOW_ONCE state but exposes no production effect-consumption path; any V1D consumer requires a separate ADR.

decisionQuestion: What exact V1C privileged architecture should MIHVER adopt for the Authorization Ledger, human R3 AuthorizationGrant administration, trusted Council/evidence import boundary, and persistent global stopEpoch register, while preserving strict privilege separation and guaranteeing zero execution-effect consumers? This is a NEW candidate (decision-4); the prior candidate (decisionHash sha256:540531...b6e9f3) was REJECTED by seat-openai and is permanently closed -- do not resubmit it, cosmetically rename it, or reuse its architecture unless materially revised.
evidence: MANDATORY: your candidate MUST NOT claim 'zero execution consumers' while also describing any downstream execution-tier consumption flow. ALLOW_ONCE/checkAndConsume may exist as privileged state only; no production component may consume it to perform an effect in V1C. A future V1D handoff must be described only as a dormant interface requiring a separate ADR.

MANDATORY: define stopEpoch's exact privileged owner, serialized/transactional increment mechanism, restart persistence, corruption/ambiguity handling, stale-epoch rejection, and why no normal ADMIN/CLIENT API can decrement or reset it.

MANDATORY: define mechanically enforceable privilege separation: process identity, OS user/group, ADMIN vs CLIENT capability split, filesystem ownership, IPC permissions, trusted-registry mutation authority, evidence import authority, grant issuance authority, stopEpoch mutation authority. 'Logically separate' alone is insufficient.

Baseline to evaluate: a dedicated privileged Authorization Ledger service, structurally separate from Publication Broker, with its own OS identity, separate ADMIN and CLIENT Unix-domain sockets with filesystem permissions and OS peer-credential checks, SQLite/WAL transactional storage, a trusted CouncilEpochRegistry, canonical privileged-validated evidence import (never trusting caller-supplied hash-shaped artifacts by default), persistent monotonic stopEpoch, exact-bound AuthorizationGrant records, a consume-once ledger, and transactional audit -- with ZERO production consumer of checkAndConsume/ALLOW_ONCE at V1C exit. You may select a different design only if you explain why it is materially safer or simpler for MIHVER's actual local single-machine threat model.

Do NOT select HSM/TPM/enclave/hypervisor isolation/M-of-N human ceremony/Merkle-SMT state/air-gap/distributed consensus unless you name a concrete threat that simpler local OS-level privilege separation (dedicated OS user, Unix socket peer-credential checks, SQLite WAL, filesystem permissions) does not adequately mitigate. Prefer least privilege, deterministic correctness, crash safety, auditability, small attack surface, and implementability over mechanisms that merely sound stronger.

Claude and Codex must never hold ADMIN capability or credentials, must never be able to create an AuthorizationGrant, alter the trusted Council registry, or change stopEpoch, under any circumstance in your design.
Keep your JSON payload concise and concrete enough that a fresh implementation team could implement it without reopening basic trust-boundary decisions, but do not include chain-of-thought.
